final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative hydrophobic substitution with high PLM (1.0) and structure compatibility (0.957), plus positive evolutionary tolerance; supports improved receptor binding or fusion potential.
Top structure compatibility (0.982) and maximum PLM support this aliphatic substitution in the head domain, likely to enhance structural stability without disrupting function.
Strong protein-level signals (structure and PLM) outweigh absence in homologs; conservative V->I is plausible to improve cell entry via enhanced structural compatibility.

stop_reason.detail: The evidence already provides clear support for the top three mutations and no phenotype tool is available to further differentiate them.

history.rationale: Buried methionine in a beta-propeller blade; substituting Leu reduces side-chain entropy while retaining hydrophobic packing. This should improve head-domain stability and cell-surface G levels, supporting fusion.
No evidence yet; retain based on initial heuristic confidence.
High PLM (1.0) and structure compatibility (0.957) with positive evolutionary tolerance support this conservative substitution as viable and potentially beneficial for cell entry.

Conservative beta-branched hydrophobic substitution at a likely buried position can tighten core packing. Increased stability of the G head is expected to preserve receptor binding and improve fusion competence.
No evidence yet; retain based on initial heuristic confidence.
Top structure compatibility (0.982) and max PLM strongly support this aliphatic substitution in the head domain.

Isoleucine to leucine at a buried hydrophobic core position is generally well tolerated and can slightly reduce steric strain. This may stabilize the folded attachment domain without altering the receptor-binding surface.
No evidence yet; retain based on initial heuristic confidence.
Positive evolutionary tolerance and moderate PLM, but weak structure compatibility lowers utility for cell entry.

Valine to isoleucine adds one methyl group in a hydrophobic environment, often improving core packing. This conservative change could increase thermostability and help maintain an active prefusion G conformation.
No evidence yet; retain based on initial heuristic confidence.
Strong protein-level signals (structure and PLM) outweigh absence in homologs; conservative V->I is plausible for function despite evolutionary novelty.

Conservative isoleucine-to-leucine substitution at a core position may reduce local flexibility while preserving hydrophobicity. A more rigid beta-propeller head could enhance receptor-triggered fusogenic transitions.
No evidence yet; retain based on initial heuristic confidence.
Max PLM but moderate structure compatibility and no evolutionary evidence leave this candidate middle-ranked.

Lysine-to-arginine preserves positive charge and likely maintains or slightly improves electrostatic interactions in the receptor-proximal region. Arginine can form additional hydrogen bonds, potentially improving ephrin engagement and cell entry.
No evidence yet; retain based on initial heuristic confidence.
Moderate structure and PLM support but low evolutionary signal and borderline coverage reduce confidence.

Isoleucine-to-leucine is a conservative hydrophobic substitution that may stabilize the local core without perturbing nearby loops. Enhanced packing in this region could improve G surface expression and fusion promotion.
No evidence yet; retain based on initial heuristic confidence.
High structure compatibility (0.939) and good PLM support, despite no homolog occurrence, indicating a potentially stabilizing mutation.
Valine-to-isoleucine at a buried position can fill a small cavity and improve hydrophobic contacts. This may increase the stability of the attachment domain and preserve efficient G-mediated entry.
No evidence yet; retain based on initial heuristic confidence.
Very low structure compatibility and limited evolutionary coverage outweigh strong PLM signal.

Conservative hydrophobic substitution near the C-terminal part of the ectodomain could stabilize local secondary structure. Maintaining the fold in this region is important for receptor recognition and fusion activation.
No evidence yet; retain based on initial heuristic confidence.
Low structure compatibility, no evolutionary evidence, and limited coverage make this the least attractive candidate.

Glutamate-to-glutamine removes a negative charge while preserving side-chain length and hydrogen-bonding capacity. If E509 lies in a strained surface loop, this change could reduce electrostatic repulsion and modestly improve fusogenic activity.
No evidence yet; retain based on initial heuristic confidence.
Decent structure and PLM but lack of homolog occurrence and low coverage reduce confidence.
